metrics.label: Food basket
metrics.title: Is the global food bill rising?
metrics.description: A broad measure of internationally traded food prices. It shows whether pressure is spreading across the food basket.
metrics.why: The headline outcome: a persistent rise across food categories would support the case for a wider price shock.
metrics.caveat: Export-weighted commodity prices, not supermarket prices. Energy, trade policy and currencies also matter. Recent meat prices include estimates and the index can be revised.
metrics.mechanism: Regional harvest losses → tighter internationally traded supplies → a more expensive food basket.
metrics.assumptions: Peak uplifts of 5%, 15% and 30% by June 2027. By August 2029, prices are 4%, 8% and 15% above the frozen anchor. These are judgement-based total-price scenarios, not estimates of the portion caused by El Niño.

metrics.label: Rice
metrics.title: The price of a staple
metrics.description: Rice connects Asian growing conditions with the food bills of import-dependent countries.
metrics.why: Rice connects Asian growing conditions with the food bills of import-dependent countries.
metrics.mechanism: Drought in exposed Asian growing regions → lower rice availability → pressure on export prices.
metrics.caveat: Export restrictions, government stocks and exchange rates can dominate weather effects. One benchmark does not represent all rice varieties.
metrics.assumptions: At the 2027-06 peak checkpoint, low / medium / high paths are +0% / +18% / +40% versus the frozen anchor. Paths then allow supply recovery; endpoint assumptions are available below. These are judgement-based stress scenarios, not fitted forecasts.

metrics.label: Maize
metrics.title: From the harvest to the feed bill
metrics.description: Maize is both a staple and animal feed, connecting harvest conditions with meat and dairy costs.
metrics.why: Maize is both a staple and animal feed, connecting harvest conditions with meat and dairy costs.
metrics.mechanism: Poor harvests → tighter grain and feed supplies → higher costs across the food chain.
metrics.caveat: This global benchmark may stay stable while southern African prices rise. US harvests, ethanol demand and Black Sea trade are major influences.
metrics.assumptions: At the 2027-06 peak checkpoint, low / medium / high paths are -3% / +12% / +30% versus the frozen anchor. Paths then allow supply recovery; endpoint assumptions are available below. These are judgement-based stress scenarios, not fitted forecasts.

metrics.label: Sugar
metrics.title: A sweet crop, a volatile market
metrics.description: Sugar adds a weather-sensitive ingredient used widely in processed food.
metrics.why: Sugar adds a weather-sensitive ingredient used widely in processed food.
metrics.mechanism: Stress in cane-growing regions → less sugar available for export → higher ingredient costs.
metrics.caveat: Brazilian harvests, ethanol economics and trade policy can offset or intensify losses elsewhere.
metrics.assumptions: At the 2027-06 peak checkpoint, low / medium / high paths are -5% / +20% / +45% versus the frozen anchor. Paths then allow supply recovery; endpoint assumptions are available below. These are judgement-based stress scenarios, not fitted forecasts.

metrics.label: Palm oil
metrics.title: Pressure in the cooking-oil market
metrics.description: A key cooking oil and food ingredient, with production exposed to Southeast Asian weather.
metrics.why: A key cooking oil and food ingredient, with production exposed to Southeast Asian weather.
metrics.mechanism: Water stress in oil-palm regions → delayed production losses → tighter edible-oil supplies.
metrics.caveat: Biodiesel mandates, competing vegetable oils and export policies also influence the price. Production effects can arrive with a lag.
metrics.assumptions: At the 2027-09 peak checkpoint, low / medium / high paths are +0% / +18% / +35% versus the frozen anchor. Paths then allow supply recovery; endpoint assumptions are available below. These are judgement-based stress scenarios, not fitted forecasts.

metrics.label: Coffee
metrics.title: What happens to the morning coffee?
metrics.description: Robusta offers a focused link to drought exposure in Vietnam and a familiar household purchase.
metrics.why: Robusta offers a focused link to drought exposure in Vietnam and a familiar household purchase.
metrics.mechanism: Hot, dry growing conditions → lower Robusta supply → pressure on wholesale coffee prices.
metrics.caveat: Wholesale beans are only part of the retail price. Stocks, Brazilian supply, currencies and the preceding price cycle can outweigh new weather damage.
metrics.assumptions: At the 2027-06 peak checkpoint, low / medium / high paths are -10% / +20% / +50% versus the frozen anchor. Paths then allow supply recovery; endpoint assumptions are available below. These are judgement-based stress scenarios, not fitted forecasts.

metrics.label: UK groceries
metrics.title: Does the shock reach the checkout?
metrics.description: The price level of food and non-alcoholic drinks bought by UK households.
metrics.why: The final link in the chain: do higher commodity costs reach the household food bill?
metrics.mechanism: Imported ingredients → manufacturing and distribution costs → household food prices.
metrics.caveat: UK only. Sterling, wages, energy and retailer margins all affect this index. Falling inflation does not mean falling prices.
metrics.assumptions: By December 2027: low +3%, medium +7%, high +12% versus July 2026. By August 2029: +7%, +12%, +20%. All are cumulative price-level changes, not annual inflation rates or causal estimates.

metrics.label: El Niño
metrics.title: The Pacific signal behind the story
metrics.description: Three-month relative sea-surface temperature anomalies in the Niño 3.4 region. Each point is dated to the middle month of its season.
metrics.why: Tracks the climate driver. Greater strength raises the risk of impacts, but does not guarantee damage in every region.
metrics.mechanism: Warmer relative Pacific temperatures → shifted rainfall patterns → changing risks for growing regions.
metrics.caveat: RONI adjusts for tropical background warming; do not compare it directly with unadjusted Niño 3.4 values. Recent observations are provisional. Climate scenarios stop in July 2027.
metrics.assumptions: Illustrative strength paths peak in November 2026 at 2.0°C / 2.6°C / 3.0°C, then decline to −0.2°C / 0.3°C / 1.0°C in July 2027. The official August NOAA outlook informs the peak range; these paths are our conditional illustrations, not NOAA forecast quantiles.

metrics.label: Maize harvest
metrics.title: The harvest on the front line
metrics.description: Annual maize yield in South Africa, an exposed producer and regional supplier. Points use USDA marketing-year labels, not calendar-month observations.
metrics.why: Tests the physical harvest link. In this panel, a lower line means a higher impact.
metrics.mechanism: Summer heat and drought → lower yields → less maize for domestic use and regional exports.
metrics.caveat: Historical points are USDA estimates and remain revisable. The separate 2026/27 USDA forecast is 5.50 tonnes/ha; it is not shown as an observed harvest. A local crop loss does not imply a global shortage.
metrics.assumptions: 2026/27 yields: low-impact 5.9, medium 5.5, high-impact 4.3 tonnes/ha. The medium scenario matches the archived USDA forecast. Subsequent seasons assume recovery; high impact means lower yield. Annual paths are illustrative, not monthly forecasts.
